plain.li: Easy now. Easy.
There you go. That's it.
Hold still, you great lump.
[job:milk] Steady, girl. Nearly done.
[job:milk] Don't you dare kick that bucket.
[job:milk] Warm hands, I promise. Mostly.
[job:shear] You'll feel lighter, I swear it.
[job:shear] Stop wriggling or you'll get a haircut you'll regret.
[job:shear,summer] There. Cooler already, aren't you?
[job:tame] Nobody's going to hurt you. Look, I've got food.
[job:tame] Come on. Just a little closer.
[job:tame,wild] I know. I know. I'd be wary too.
[job:train] Again. And again. Good!
[job:train] Sit. No. Sit. Sit! ... Close enough.
[job:train,named] {PET_nameDef}, look at me. Look. Good.
[job:tend] This will sting. Sorry. Sorry.
[job:tend] Brave thing. Nearly done.
[job:feed] Slowly. It isn't going anywhere.
[job:rescue] Up you come. I've got you.
[job:rope] Come on, home. This way. Home.
[job:rope] No, the other way. The pen's the other way.
[childplay] Do you want to be my friend? You can be my friend.
[childplay] Shh. Stay still. I'm going to pat you very gently.
[childplay] Want to hear a secret? It's about the cook.
[childplay,young] You're just a baby. Like me. Well. Not like me.
[bonded,named] Who's my best friend? You are, {PET_nameDef}. Don't tell the others.
[bonded] I'm here. I'm always here.
[young] Look at those legs. You'll grow into them.
[oldanimal] Slow and steady, old friend. No hurry.
[oldanimal,named] Still the best of them, aren't you, {PET_nameDef}?
[pokemon] Ready? Good. Let's work on that move again.
[pokemon] Back in the ball after this, all right? Then berries.
[pokemon,job:tend] A potion would be better. You'll have to make do with me.
[winter] Cold hands, sorry. Cold everything.
[rain] I know, I'm wet too. Nearly done.
[night] Shh. Everyone's asleep. Just us.

warm.li: Good animal. You're such a good animal.
[bonded] There's nobody I'd rather spend the morning with.

cheerful.li: Who's a clever one? You're a clever one!
[job:shear] Look at you. All fluffy, and then not!

gloomy.li: At least you don't complain about the food.
[oldanimal] We're both getting old, you and me.

plain.li: Come on then, {PET_nameDef}. You can help.
Where I go, you go, is that it?
All right, {PET_nameDef}. Keep up.
You're underfoot again. I don't mind.
[night] Bedtime, {PET_nameDef}? All right. Me too.
[rain] You'll be soaked. Come on, then.
[pokemon] Out of the ball and straight to my heels. Good.
[working] I've got work to do. Fine. You can watch.

warm.li: There you are. I was wondering where you'd got to.

cheerful.li: Adventure time, {PET_nameDef}! Probably to the storeroom.

gloomy.li: At least somebody wants my company.

plain.li: There. That's the best sound in the colony.
One, two, three... they're all here.
Just sitting. Just watching them eat.
[child] Can I name that one? I'm naming that one.
[evening] They always settle down at dusk. So do I.
[spring] Look at the young ones go.
[winter] Huddled up, all of them. Sensible.

warm.li: Hello, all of you. Did you have a good day?

cheerful.li: Best seats in the colony, right here.

gloomy.li: They don't worry about anything. I'd like to learn how.

plain.li: Stand still and I'll get the burrs out.
Look at the state of you. Rolled in something, did you?
[named] Hold still, {OTHER_nameDef}. Nearly there.
[bonded] There's my favourite. Let's get you shining.
[winter] Thick coat this year. Good. You'll need it.
[summer] Shedding everywhere. On me, mostly.

warm.li: You like that, don't you? Behind the ears. I know.

cheerful.li: Who's going to be the handsomest animal in the colony?

gloomy.li: Somebody should look after you properly. Might as well be me.

cold.li: Grooming reduces skin trouble. Hold still.

plain.li: [named] Welcome to the herd, {PET_nameDef}.
[named] {PET_nameDef}. Yes. You look like a {PET_nameDef}.
[named] There. You've a name now, {PET_nameDef}. Look after your mother.
[nonamed] Hello, little one. Welcome.
[nonamed] Already on your feet. Good.

warm.li: [named] Hello, {PET_nameDef}. We're all very glad you're here.

cheerful.li: [named] {PET_nameDef}. Best name I've thought of all year!

cold.li: [named] {PET_nameDef}. Healthy, by the look of you.

plain.li: [named] A young {KIND} born to {OTHER_nameDef} last night. I went down at first light and named it {PET_nameDef}.
[named] New in the herd: {PET_nameDef}, all legs. {OTHER_nameDef} wouldn't let me near for an hour.
[nonamed] A young one born to {OTHER_nameDef}. On its feet within the hour, which is how it should be.
[winter,named] Born in the cold, {PET_nameDef}. I put extra straw down and stayed until it was feeding.

warm.li: [named] {PET_nameDef}, the newest of us. I sat in the straw a long time just watching it breathe.

cheerful.li: [named] Welcome, {PET_nameDef}. The herd keeps growing and I keep running out of names!

cold.li: [named] One birth in the herd, a young {KIND}, named {PET_nameDef}. Mother and young both well.

plain.li: [sick] {PAWN_nameDef}, the herdmaster, found {OTHER_nameDef} after work to say that {PET_nameDef} was eating again, a little.
[sick] {PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} what {PET_nameDef}'s illness was and what to watch for, and promised to look in at night.
[hurt] {PAWN_nameDef} came by to tell {OTHER_nameDef} that {PET_nameDef}'s wound was clean and closing.
[hurt] {PAWN_nameDef} showed {OTHER_nameDef} how to change {PET_nameDef}'s dressing, and stayed while {OTHER_pronoun} tried.
{PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} went down to see {PET_nameDef} together, and {PAWN_nameDef} said it would mend.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} found {OTHER_nameDef} worrying by the pens and stayed until {OTHER_pronoun} stopped, talking about {PET_nameDef} the whole time.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} that {PET_nameDef} would live, and to go and get some sleep.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} gave {OTHER_nameDef} a plain account of {PET_nameDef}'s condition. It was better than {OTHER_nameDef} had feared.

plain.li: [first] A year ago today the colony's first young {SUBJECT} was born, and {A_nameDef} sat up all night with it. {A_nameDef} wants the day marked.
[years] {YEARS} years since the first young {SUBJECT} was born to the herd. There have been many since. {A_nameDef} still remembers the first.
The day of the first foal. {A_nameDef} has hung a wreath on the gate of the pens.
[tradition] The first foal's day, and the herd gets an extra measure of feed, as every year. So do the people.
[spring] The first foal's day, with young ones in the pens again. {A_nameDef} says the herd remembers too.

cheerful.li: The first foal's day! {A_nameDef} has baked something in the shape of the first {SUBJECT}. It looks like a loaf.

cold.li: The anniversary of the herd's first birth. {A_nameDef} notes the herd has grown since. A meal seems in order.

plain.li: [new] The first young {SUBJECT} born to our herd. I was there. Wet, wobbling, alive. The herd is a real herd now.
[new] Something born here, to animals we keep. It feels like the colony took root a little deeper today.
[!new,first] A year since our first foal. It's grown, and so have we.
[!new,years] {YEARS} years since the first foal. I went down to the pens at dawn, as I do on this day.
[!new,tradition] The first foal's day, kept as always: a wreath on the gate, a feast in the evening.

warm.li: [new] I held it while it found its legs. I'll remember that for the rest of my life.

cheerful.li: [new] Our first baby animal. I want to name it everything!

gloomy.li: [new] A new life in the pens. I hope this place is kind to it.

cold.li: [new] The herd has bred for the first time. The colony's food is a little more secure.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} about the night the first foal was born, and how long it took to stand.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} went to look at the herd together and tried to work out which of them came from the first foal.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} what {B_pronoun} remembered of the first foal's night.
[first] A year ago today {DEAD} died. {A_nameDef} has been quiet since breakfast, and went out to the place where {DEAD} used to sleep in the sun.
[years] It's {YEARS} years since {DEAD} died. {A_nameDef} still keeps the old collar on a nail by the bed.
{DEAD}'s day. {A_nameDef} saved the best scraps from supper and left them on the grave, the way {DEAD} would have wanted.
[tradition] Every year on this day the colony remembers {DEAD}, the best {SUBJECT} there ever was, and {A_nameDef} tells the story of how they met.
[winter] {DEAD}'s day, and snow on the grave. {A_nameDef} cleared it by hand.

warm.li: It's {DEAD}'s day. {A_nameDef} has been telling the children what kind of {SUBJECT} {DEAD} was, so that someone new remembers.

blunt.li: {DEAD}'s day. {A_nameDef} went to the grave and came back without a word.

plain.li: [first] A year since {DEAD} died. I still look down for {DEAD} at the door.
[years] {YEARS} years without {DEAD}. Some days it feels like a lot longer, some days like last week.
{DEAD}'s day. I sat where {DEAD} used to sleep and told {DEAD} about the year. It's silly. I did it anyway.
[tradition] {DEAD}'s day, kept as always. There's a new {SUBJECT} in the colony now, and it came and sat with me.

warm.li: {DEAD}'s day. I'm grateful for every year we had. I wish we'd had more.

cheerful.li: {DEAD}'s day. I told all the {DEAD} stories at supper and everyone laughed in the right places.

gloomy.li: {DEAD}'s day. Nothing has been quite as good since.

cold.li: {DEAD}'s day. I marked it. I find I still miss {DEAD} more than I expected.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} about {DEAD}, and the time {DEAD} stole a whole ham off the table.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} walked out to {DEAD}'s grave together and stood there a while.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} if {B_pronoun} remembered {DEAD}, and {B_nameDef} did, every bit of it.
